card.name: Gadhika
card.tagline: Adiya healing ritual to appease angry gods
card.profile: Gadhika (also Gaddika) is a ritual art of the Adiya (Adiyor) scheduled-tribe community of Wayanad district, Kerala, performed to cure disease and ward off misfortune and the evil eye (Wikipedia; Kerala Tourism). The tribe believes that sickness arises from divine displeasure, so the chief priest (Gaddikakaran/Moopan), dressed in red, invokes Lord Shiva, after which deities such as Chamundi, Maniamma, Malamkali and Karimkali are believed to arrive (Kerala Tourism). The dialect blends Kannada and Tulu; it has two forms - public Naattu Gadhika and ritualistic Pooja Gadhika (the latter performed to cure illness or for the safe delivery of a child) - accompanied by wind instruments and drums, often in the Malayalam month of Mithunam (June-July) (Wikipedia; Kerala Tourism).
card.insight: Under the leadership of the Adiya Mooppan and politician P. K. Kalan, Gadhika - once purely ritual - was brought to public platforms inside and outside Kerala without losing its artistic values, and the Kerala Scheduled Tribes Development Department's tribal art fair is named 'Gadhika' in its honour (Wikipedia).

observation.setting: outdoor courtyard at night with dirt floor, near a simple dwelling and trees
observation.dancers: group of older women and men, mixed group with musicians and observers standing in the background
observation.formation_and_space: circle formation moving in a counterclockwise direction around a central ritual arrangement on the ground
observation.posture: slightly bent forward from the waist with soft, flexed knees
observation.footwork: stepping rhythmically on the beat, moving side-to-side and pivoting in a circle
observation.arms_and_hands: holding hands in a circle initially, later some dancers hold long wooden walking sticks or sway arms
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal isolated movements, torso maintains a slight forward inclination with gentle bouncing on the beat
observation.partnering: hand-in-hand circle formation with no lead-and-follow partnering
observation.levels_jumps_turns: low level with frequent bending of the knees towards the ground, circular turns while maintaining circle formation
observation.costume_and_props: women wear brightly colored saris with red head coverings and scarves; some hold walking sticks; background men wear white dhotis and red shawls
observation.cannot_infer: fast footwork and exact weight transfer are obscured by low video resolution and lighting

signature_moments.what: dancers in a circle bend low toward the center while holding hands, then rise and pivot around
